neighbours.label: the connective (and / then / please / simply / comma) that pivots into the next imperative step of a software or navigation instruction, not the same subject matter reported as narrative
fire: Open the account page in your browser, and click Manage Subscriptions near the bottom.
Locate the message in your inbox, then choose Forward from the toolbar.
To update your address, sign in to the portal and select Edit Profile.
If the download stalls, please click Retry rather than refreshing the page.
Choose the photo you want to crop, then drag the corner handles inward.
Once the installer opens, simply click Next and accept the default location.
Find the row for last month, and select Download as CSV from the menu.
To leave the group, open the member list and tap Leave Group at the bottom.
quiet: Her account page loaded slowly, and the subscription list never appeared at all.
He found the message in his inbox, but the attachment had already expired.
The portal lost my new address twice before the clerk fixed it by hand.
The download stalled at ninety percent and the log blamed the proxy server.
She cropped the photo on her phone and sent it to the printer that evening.
The installer opened a second window and offered a toolbar nobody wanted.
The report for last month arrived as a spreadsheet with three empty columns.
He left the group quietly and nobody noticed until the next meeting.

predictions: Fires on the connective introducing a second imperative in click-here instructions; the same topics written as past-tense description stay low.
short: pivot into the next step of a UI instruction
notes: Card: ' and' x9, ',' x5, ' can' x5, ' please' x2, ' then' x2; top examples are all click/go instructions. Probe: 'then select Share' 0.711, 'and click Security' 0.642, 'simply click Checkout' 0.642, 'please click the link' 0.439; narrative 'shared and smiled' 0.315 and physical instructions 0.210 are the closest misses, so near misses are descriptive rather than physical-imperative.
